steps.what: Initiate and moderate classroom discussions while facilitating respectful, evidence-based participation

tasks.design: Retain live discussion facilitation, using {DOCS} readings as shared reference material. The teacher responds to actual contributions and helps students examine competing perspectives.
tasks.previous_blocker: Useful moderation depends on what students say and how others receive it.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing reading access supports context without replacing facilitation.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive identity topics and unequal participation require contextual judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher recognizes exclusion, uncertainty and productive disagreement.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in classroom facilitation responsibility or time.

reach.task: Help learners articulate and question an interpretation

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: live cultural studies discussion retains human facilitation time; no shorter equivalent interaction is established.

assumptions: Boundary is moderated discussion, excluding lecture delivery, course-material production and assessment.
Students produce contributions during the session; the teacher interprets them during counted s1. No participation, emotion or understanding flag is assumed available.
Use existing reading libraries before custom discussion support.
Zero incremental upkeep because no recording, model or additional reporting process is introduced.
research_questions: Can existing prompts improve participation while preserving live discussion time?

tasks.short: Evaluate cultural studies papers and assignments

steps.what: Evaluate students' use of sources, interpretation and reasoning against assignment criteria
Draft feedback explaining the assessment and useful directions for revision

loop.purpose: Compose feedback from the teacher's specific assessment
loop.input: Teacher notes, criteria and quoted student passages
loop.check: Verify the student's position is represented fairly and each criticism reflects the teacher's evidence and judgement
loop.stop: One draft and correction; unsupported feedback is written manually
loop.why_not_simpler: Feedback on varied interpretations requires contextual prose beyond fixed comments

steps.what: Set the grade and finalize comments for the evaluated work

tasks.design: Use {LMS} feedback drafting from teacher-authored assessment notes while retaining close reading and grade decisions. The teacher checks whether comments fairly represent the student's position and finalizes every assessment.
tasks.previous_blocker: Writing specific feedback repeated points already established in teacher notes.
tasks.enabler_now: Instructor-note-based drafting can suggest wording for correction.
tasks.still_hard: Competing interpretations and culturally situated evidence need careful judgement.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher can recognize a well-supported interpretation without requiring agreement with it.
tasks.altitude: A little composition time returns to examining sources and arguments.

reach.task: Prepare passage-based feedback under examiner guidance
reach.learn: Rubric calibration and fair representation of arguments

evidence.claim: D2L Brightspace Lumi Feedback drafts feedback from instructor notes; this does not establish autonomous grades or measured cultural studies savings.
Model knowledge: the checked-feedback labour estimate is an unmeasured scenario.

assumptions: Boundary covers non-exam work assessment, excluding examination marking and official grade transfer.

The teacher produces s1 notes with submission version, criterion, quoted passage, judgement and intended advice. Capture and reading stay fully counted; missing evidence or unclear interpretation prompts manual comments rather than model-assigned grades.
Test native feedback functions and existing comment banks before custom tools.
Four incremental focal hours cover instruction review and sample audits.
unknowns: Existing feedback tools and approved uses
research_questions: Does checked drafting preserve fair representation of different interpretations while reducing total feedback time?

approvals.approved_version: Exact student submission, criteria, final grade and comments; changes void approval

time_saved_range_pct.basis: E1 B100 R93.75 gives6.25 gross minus4 upkeep =2.25 net. Brief comments or nuanced arguments needing complete rewriting support only0-1% conservative saving.

tasks.short: Prepare and deliver cultural studies lectures

steps.what: Prepare lecture sequence and examples from established course material and current scholarship
Deliver lectures on cultural perspectives and clarify questions arising during instruction

tasks.design: Use prepared material in {DOCS} while the teacher chooses the lecture sequence and delivers explanations personally. Reusable material drafting belongs to the separate course-material task, so its savings are counted there once.
tasks.previous_blocker: Lecture preparation requires deciding which distinctions and examples this class needs.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing materials support preparation without establishing less delivery or rehearsal time.
tasks.still_hard: Sensitive examples and misunderstood concepts need responsive explanation.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher connects scholarship to the learners' actual questions and prior understanding.
tasks.altitude: Nothing changes in lecture preparation judgement or delivery time; material-production savings are separate.

reach.task: Sequence concepts for a particular class

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: selecting the lecture approach and delivering instruction retain human time; separate reusable material production is not saved twice.

assumptions: Boundary covers lecture sequencing, rehearsal and delivery, excluding reusable syllabi, handouts and homework production as well as separately moderated discussions.

The course-material author produces checked teaching material before lecture preparation. The teacher verifies relevance and chooses examples during counted s1; students produce questions during s2, never before delivery.
Use native document and teaching tools before custom support.
Zero incremental upkeep because this task introduces no new automation or additional recurring process.
research_questions: Can the boundary between reusable material production and actual lecture preparation be measured without overlap?

already_counted.description: Choose lecture approach and rehearse explanations

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B100 R100 gross0 upkeep0 net0. Reused lectures and classes needing fresh explanations retain sequencing and contact time; drafting gains belong to course materials only.

steps.what: Specify course materials, outcomes, readings and assignment requirements
Prepare syllabi, homework instructions and handouts from the specified material brief

loop.purpose: Draft reusable course documents within explicit teaching requirements
loop.input: Material brief, templates and selected source passages
loop.output: Course material draft with source references and gaps
loop.check: Verify source meaning, representation of groups, instructions, workload and alignment to outcomes
loop.stop: One draft and correction; ambiguous instructions or unsupported claims return to manual writing
loop.why_not_simpler: Source-based explanations and assignment instructions vary beyond template fields

steps.what: Verify sources and finalize the course materials for release

tasks.design: Start with {DOCS} templates and reusable sources, then draft prose through a bounded loop. The teacher checks cultural context, source accuracy and instructions before finalizing materials in {LMS}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Producing consistent course documents required repeated manual composition.
tasks.enabler_now: Source-bound drafting can create provisional documents for substantive teacher review.
tasks.still_hard: Apparently clear wording can simplify contested perspectives or make assignments inaccessible.
tasks.human_edge: The teacher selects fair, relevant material and anticipates how students will interpret instructions.
tasks.altitude: Some repetitive composition time returns to checking sources and assignment design.

reach.task: Check the alignment of course documents and outcomes
reach.learn: Accessible assignment design and source-context review

evidence.claim: Model knowledge: bounded drafting of source-based course documents is plausible; the supplied digest does not establish this task's local labour saving.

assumptions: Boundary covers reusable syllabus, homework and handout production, excluding lecture sequencing and delivery, curriculum decisions and student marking. Documents are produced once and their gains allocated here.

The teacher creates s1 outcomes, class level, source versions, permitted passages, assessment instructions, dates and accessibility requirements. Capture and selection stay counted; missing dates or uncertain source claims require manual completion rather than inferred fields.
Test native templates and existing reusable content before custom drafting; calendar fields can remain deterministic.
Six incremental focal hours cover source updates and document-template checks.
unknowns: Existing material reuse and document standards
research_questions: Does checked drafting reduce document production while preserving source context and unambiguous assignment requirements?

approvals.approved_version: Exact syllabus, homework and handout versions, sources, dates and instructions; changes void approval
